title: Never Let the Model See the Secret: Zero Data Retention Is Not Enough
content_md: TL;DR Nearly 2 million prompts, 2,000 routes, 3 leaking providers: Dragos sent nearly 2 million canary prompts and traced about 2,000 routes. At least three AI providers leaked secrets, and none knew until told. One lab pulled secret links from roughly two-thirds of the prompts flagged Zero Data Retention. Tens of thousands of API calls, some within hours: Stolen AWS keys drew tens of thousands of API calls, some within hours, and attackers confirmed keys with ARTEX. Every employee with an AI assistant is now one paste away from feeding that pipeline. You only control the first hop : Rotate anything that may have been pasted, then stop the next one at the laptop. AI Hooks block secrets before a model, router, or reseller ever sees them. The moment a credential enters an AI prompt, your attack surface extends to every company involved in processing it. Dragos just proved that for some model providers, guarantees around Zero Data Retention (ZDR) were like writing "don't mess up" in the prompt; they were just suggestions that could be ignored. In late November, HD Moore, Chief Research Officer at Dragos, published research on what happened to secrets after they are entered into an AI prompt. For months, his team sent nearly 2 million prompts to widely used AI services, each one carrying a unique, trackable secret.
